author: Russell Brand
description:
Why does sin feel so good at first, only to leave us feeling worse afterward? author: Russell Brand
description:
Why did Jesus have to suffer in the Garden of Gethsemane before His crucifixion? Russell Brand and his guests explore the mystery of Christ's human and divine nature, questioning why Jesus experienced such profound anguish before willingly embracing the cross. Connecting His suffering to the biblical story of Jacob wrestling with God, they discuss what these moments reveal about human struggle, spiritual transformation, and the deeper purpose of suffering in God's plan.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Do scientific studies really prove a connection between vaccines and autism? Russell Brand and his guest examine controversial claims about childhood vaccination schedules, mercury exposure, and research suggesting a possible link to autism. From disputed statistics to the differences between retrospective studies and clinical trials, they explore what the evidence actually establishes and whether correlation can demonstrate causation.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Was Joseph's betrayal actually a kind of crucifixion? Russell Brand explores the biblical story of Joseph being stripped of his robe, thrown into a cistern by his brothers, and eventually sold into slavery for twenty pieces of silver. But could the cistern represent something far deeper than imprisonment? Russell suggests that Joseph's suffering symbolizes the death of his old identity and the beginning of a spiritual transformation, before exploring how biblical stories might reveal a reality beyond space and time — and offer us a glimpse into eternity.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Could the Bible have been describing extraterrestrial beings all along? Timothy Alberino explores the possibility that angels, the “sons of God,” and the “morning stars” are references to intelligent beings that existed long before humanity. He suggests that the Kingdom of Heaven is an ancient civilization beyond our own, and that the biblical account of Armageddon may describe something far greater than a human conflict — the final battle in a cosmic war against God.
